subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose explicit child-topic native subagent session spawning now, while keeping normal Telegram top-level binding on the current conversation or topic by default?
rationale: The remaining behavior affects visible Telegram topic creation, plugin capability/API shape, model-visible spawn affordances, and session/message routing defaults, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve the API and visibility blockers, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep current-conversation Telegram binding only and leave this issue open until maintainers decide the child-topic visibility and API model.

options.title: Reject Telegram child-topic spawning
options.body: Close this issue and associated candidate PRs if maintainers decide native subagent work should not create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve the API and visibility blockers, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice sits on the core session-binding adapter path introduced by this owner and crosses Telegram/plugin routing boundaries.
